# Peking University 在声明样本中的研究全景：DistServe（OSDI '24）候选记录

> 按本次所选研究模块组织；来源摘述和分析仍需阅读审核状态。

## 研究全景

**来源摘述（待审核）**：本次样本仅包含一个种子出版页，即 USENIX OSDI '24 的 DistServe 论文页；来源域限定为 usenix\.org，输出类型限定为 conference\_paper，时间窗为 2024\-07\-16 至 2024\-07\-31。因此，下文只描述这一声明样本，不代表 Peking University 系统研究的全集，也不能把样本中的篇数解释为投入或产出规模。 [citation:1]

**来源摘述（待审核）**：该页面的主作品为《DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput\-optimized Large Language Model Serving》，收录于 18th USENIX Symposium on Operating Systems Design and Implementation \(OSDI 24\)，页码 193–210，会议地点为 Santa Clara, CA。作者列表显示，Yinmin Zhong、Shengyu Liu、Jianbo Hu、Xuanzhe Liu、Xin Jin 的署名机构为 Peking University，Junda Chen 与 Hao Zhang 的署名机构为 UC San Diego，Yibo Zhu 的署名机构为 StepFun。也就是说，Peking University 是论文作者列表中的署名机构之一，这一署名来自论文作者列表本身，而不是个人简介或现任职信息。 [citation:1]

**分析判断（待复核）**：从摘要看，该工作属于 LLM 服务系统方向：它指出，把 prefill 与 decoding 共置并统一批处理会造成 prefill\-decoding 干扰，并耦合两阶段的资源分配与并行策略；DistServe 把两阶段分配到不同 GPU，按 TTFT/TPOT 约束协同优化资源分配与并行策略，并按集群带宽放置两阶段，以减少拆分带来的通信开销；评估称，在多种模型、应用与延迟要求下，它可以服务 7\.4× 更多请求，或支持 12\.6× 更紧的 SLO，同时让超过 90% 的请求满足延迟约束。不过，学科标签“computer science”与主题“systems research”属于请求口径，页面未提供独立的学科分类，因此不能声称已独立核实学科归属。 [citation:1]

**来源摘述（待审核）**：日期判定是本次评估的关键：出版商元数据只给出 year = \{2024\} 与 month = jul，日期精度为月，对应 2024\-07\-01 至 2024\-07\-31 的月份区间，BibTeX 中没有日字段。因此，该成果与 2024\-07\-16 至 2024\-07\-31 的窗口部分重叠，但无法确定是否落在窗口内，应保留为候选记录，并标注“日期精度不足、待核”：既不认定它在范围内，也不认定它在范围外，也不编造具体日期。类型方面，该页为 OSDI '24 会议论文（inproceedings），符合 conference\_paper 类型。 [citation:1]

**证据缺口**：待核缺口包括：精确发表日（会议日程日期）缺失；学科与主题的独立分类缺失；检索词“Harp 2026”在本次只读种子中没有任何证据，不能据此添加成果；未读取 PDF 全文，摘要页不等于全文。此外，Peking University 的实体 resolution\_status 仍为 pending，页面出现机构名可以支持署名证据，但不足以完成机构实体消歧（例如院系、重名机构）。置信度方面，标题、作者署名、venue 与月份精度日期为高（直接引自页面与 BibTeX）；“是否落入 7 月 16–31 日窗口”为低或未知（精度不足）；学科与主题核实为低（请求口径，未独立分类）。

DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
Yinmin Zhong and Shengyu Liu, Peking University; Junda Chen, UC San Diego; Jianbo Hu, Peking University; Yibo Zhu, StepFun; Xuanzhe Liu and Xin Jin, Peking University; Hao Zhang, UC San Diego
DistServe improves the performance of large language models (LLMs) serving by disaggregating the prefill and decoding computation. Existing LLM serving systems colocate the two phases and batch the computation of prefill and decoding across all users and requests. We find that this strategy not only leads to strong prefill-decoding interferences but also couples the resource allocation and parallelism plans for both phases. LLM applications often emphasize individual latency for each phase: time to first token (TTFT) for the prefill phase and time per output token (TPOT) of each request for the decoding phase. In the presence of stringent latency requirements, existing systems have to prioritize one latency over the other, or over-provision compute resources to meet both.
DistServe assigns prefill and decoding computation to different GPUs, hence eliminating prefill-decoding interferences. Given the application's TTFT and TPOT requirements, DistServe co-optimizes the resource allocation and parallelism strategy tailored for each phase. DistServe also places the two phases according to the serv

excerpts.quote:
token (TTFT) for the prefill phase and time per output token (TPOT) of each request for the decoding phase. In the presence of stringent latency requirements, existing systems have to prioritize one latency over the other, or over-provision compute resources to meet both.
DistServe assigns prefill and decoding computation to different GPUs, hence eliminating prefill-decoding interferences. Given the application's TTFT and TPOT requirements, DistServe co-optimizes the resource allocation and parallelism strategy tailored for each phase. DistServe also places the two phases according to the serving cluster's bandwidth to minimize the communication caused by disaggregation. As a result, DistServe significantly improves LLM serving performance in terms of the maximum rate that can be served within both TTFT and TPOT constraints on each GPU. Our evaluations show that on various popular LLMs, applications, and latency requirements, DistServe can serve 7.4× more requests or 12.6× tighter SLO, compared to state-of-the-art systems, while staying within latency constraints for > 90% of requests.

token (TTFT) for the prefill phase and time per output token (TPOT) of each request for the decoding phase. In the presence of stringent latency requirements, existing systems have to prioritize one latency over the other, or over-provision compute resources to meet both.
DistServe assigns prefill and decoding computation to different GPUs, hence eliminating prefill-decoding interferences. Yinmin Zhong and Shengyu Liu, Peking University; Junda Chen, UC San Diego; Jianbo Hu, Peking University; Yibo Zhu, StepFun; Xuanzhe Liu and Xin Jin, Peking University; Hao Zhang, UC San Diego
DistServe improves the performance of large language models (LLMs) serving by disaggregating the prefill and decoding computation. Existing LLM serving systems colocate the two phases and batch the computation of prefill and decoding across all users and requests. We find that this strategy not only leads to strong prefill-decoding interferences but also couples the resource allocation and parallelism plans for both phases.
